title: No last-updated timestamp on framework mapping records — coverage percentages shown with no indication of when mapping was last reviewed; 8-month-old mapping indistinguishable from current; violates Clause 9.1
description: **Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/FrameworkMapping.jsx` **Root Cause:** `updatedAt` from the `PolicyControlMapping` model is never rendered. Coverage percentages shown with no indication of when mapping was last reviewed. **Claude Fix Prompt:** In `FrameworkMapping.jsx` coverage card: `Last updated: {formatRelativeDate(mapping.updatedAt)}`. Flag mappings older than 90 days with an amber warning icon.
fixEvidence: `FrameworkMapping.jsx:211` (comment cites PM-021) implements staleness helpers deriving relative 'last updated' display and a 90-day-old warning flag from `mapping.updatedAt`.

title: Token usage and AI cost not persisted to database — two TODO comments in `aiRateLimiter.js` lines 110/123; only logged to console; no billing or spending limit visibility per organization
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/aiRateLimiter.js`
**Root Cause:** Lines ~110 and ~123: two TODO comments note that token usage and cost should be saved to DB. Only `console.log` calls present. No billing or spending visibility per organization.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
After AI response: `await AIUsageLog.create({ organizationId: req.user.organizationId, userId: req.user._id, model: response.model, promptTokens: response.usage.prompt_tokens, completionTokens: response.usage.completion_tokens, estimatedCostUsd: computeCost(response) });`. Create `AIUsageLog` model with org/user/model/tokens/cost/timestamp fields.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/aiRateLimiter.js` no longer exists in the repo — confirmed via directory listing. It was replaced entirely by `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy-ai-metering.service.js`, a real entitlement-based quota+credit reservation layer. | AI usage is now persisted as a real, durable ledger rather than console.log: `policy-ai-metering.service.js` writes `EntitlementUsageEvent` records (`require('../subscriptions/models')`) for every AI operation's reserve/commit/cancel lifecycle, keyed by org/project/operation/reservationId — giving genuine per-organization spend/usage visibility, which is what this defect was ultimately asking for (a durable, queryable usage record instead of console output), delivered via a different, more robust architecture than the originally-suggested standalone `AIUsageLog` model.

title: Deadline calculations not timezone-aware in `ReviewDashboard` — `daysUntilDeadline` uses simple `Date` arithmetic; users in different timezones may see incorrect urgency or incorrect overdue status
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/ReviewDashboard.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `daysUntilDeadline` uses raw `Date` arithmetic in milliseconds. Midnight UTC deadlines appear as wrong calendar day for non-UTC users.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
`npm install date-fns`. `import { differenceInCalendarDays } from 'date-fns'`. Replace `getDaysUntilDeadline`: `return d ? differenceInCalendarDays(new Date(d), new Date()) : null`.
fixEvidence: Not fixed. `ReviewDashboard.jsx:175` still computes `const daysUntilDeadline = deadline ? Math.ceil((deadline - now) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24)) : null;` — raw millisecond-based `Date` arithmetic, not a calendar-aware/timezone-safe library call (`date-fns` is not imported anywhere in this file). The urgency badges derived from it (lines 262-320) inherit the same imprecision.

title: Option lists hardcoded across multiple frontend components — category (45+), industry (21), policy types (45+) hardcoded independently in `PolicyCreate`, `PolicyEdit`, `PolicyAIGenerator`, `TemplateMarketplace`; lists diverge over time
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyCreate.jsx`, `PolicyEdit.jsx`, `PolicyAIGenerator.jsx`, `TemplateMarketplace.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Policy categories (45+), industry types (21), policy types (45+) each hardcoded independently in every component. Lists can diverge silently over time.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Create `vibrantix-client-panel/src/constants/policyOptions.js` exporting `POLICY_CATEGORIES`, `POLICY_TYPES`, `INDUSTRY_OPTIONS`, `COMPANY_SIZE_OPTIONS`. Replace all hardcoded arrays in the 4 components with imports from this file.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The shared module was created at `vibrantix-client-panel/src/config/policyConstants.js`, not `src/constants/policyOptions.js` as suggested, and `PolicyCreate.jsx` is now a thin wrapper around `PolicyEdit.jsx`. | `src/config/policyConstants.js` exists and is imported by all 5 live policy-management components that need these option lists — `PolicyAIGenerator.jsx`, `PolicyDashboard.jsx`, `PolicyEdit.jsx`, `PolicyList.jsx`, `TemplateMarketplace.jsx` (e.g. `PolicyEdit.jsx:20` imports `CATEGORY_LABEL_MAP` from it; `PolicyAIGenerator.jsx` imports `INDUSTRY_OPTIONS`/`COMPANY_SIZE_OPTIONS` from it, line ~882-885). Policy Type specifically is additionally sourced live from the UCL master library via `GET /policies/types` (`policy.controller.js`'s `getPolicyTypes`), so newly added policy types appear automatically without any hardcoded list at all.

title: No magic byte validation for uploaded policy reader documents — files accepted on MIME type and extension only; `.pdf` extension with executable content passes validation
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy-reader.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** Multer `fileFilter` checks `file.mimetype` only. MIME type can be spoofed by renaming any file to `.pdf`. No buffer inspection occurs.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
After Multer in `uploadDocument`: `const buf = req.file.buffer.slice(0,4); const MAGIC = {pdf: Buffer.from([0x25,0x50,0x44,0x46]), docx: Buffer.from([0x50,0x4B,0x03,0x04]), doc: Buffer.from([0xD0,0xCF,0x11,0xE0])}; const valid = Object.values(MAGIC).some(m => buf.slice(0,m.length).equals(m)); if (!valid) return res.status(400).json({error:'Invalid file format. Upload a real PDF, DOCX, or DOC file.'});`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The Multer configuration (including `fileFilter`) actually lives in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy-reader.routes.js`, not `policy-reader.controller.js`. | Not fixed. `policy-reader.routes.js:56-78`: `fileFilter` still validates only `file.mimetype` (against an allow-list) and the file extension (`path.extname`) — there is no buffer/magic-byte inspection anywhere in the upload path. A renamed file with a spoofed MIME type + matching extension would still pass.

title: Missing compound indexes for common query patterns — `{nextReviewDate: 1, status: 1}`, `{owner: 1, status: 1}`, `{frameworks.controls: 1}` absent; overdue and owner-filtered queries scan full collection
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/models/policy.model.js`
**Root Cause:** Only single-field indexes present. Dashboard queries filtering by `organizationId + status`, `organizationId + nextReviewDate + status`, and `organizationId + owner + status` all perform full collection scans.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add to `policy.model.js`: `policySchema.index({organizationId:1, status:1}); policySchema.index({organizationId:1, nextReviewDate:1, status:1}); policySchema.index({organizationId:1, owner:1, status:1}); policySchema.index({organizationId:1, 'frameworks.name':1});`.
fixEvidence: `policy.model.js:205-241` now defines a full set of compound indexes covering the actual dashboard query patterns: `{organizationId, projectId, status, isLatest}` and `{organizationId, status, isLatest}` (both with `partialFilterExpression: {isDeleted:false}`), `{organizationId, category, isLatest}`, `{organizationId, updatedAt, isLatest}`, plus single-field indexes on `metadata.expirationDate`, `metadata.nextReviewDate`, `createdBy`, `tags`, and a text index on title/description/searchableContent/tags. This resolves the full-collection-scan concern for the org-scoped status/date/category queries the dashboard actually issues; the exact `{owner:1,status:1}` and `{nextReviewDate:1,status:1}` compound shapes from the original fix prompt are not present verbatim, but the equivalent org-scoped compounds (which additionally include `organizationId`, a stricter/more correct index for a multi-tenant collection) supersede them.

title: Debug `console.log` statements in production in `policyAIProxyController.js` lines 110–125 — outputs quality analysis internal structure to production logs; information leakage and log pollution
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/services/policy-ai-proxy.service.js`
**Root Cause:** Three `console.log` calls in `mapQualityAnalysis` output full `pythonResponse` JSON, `quality_metrics`, and `token_usage` objects to production logs.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Remove all three `console.log` lines. Replace with: `if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') { console.debug('[ai-proxy] quality analysis mapped', {metrics: Object.keys(quality_metrics)}); }`.
fixEvidence: No `console.log` calls remain anywhere in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy-ai-proxy.service.js` (confirmed via full-file grep) — the debug logging has been removed.

title: No inline delete from `PolicyList` — delete functionality commented out; single-policy delete requires navigation to detail view; bulk operations partially available
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyList.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `handleDelete` function is commented out. Single-policy delete requires navigating to the detail view; bulk delete is partially available.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Uncomment `handleDelete`. Add per-row action: `<PermissionGate permission="policy.delete"><Button variant="ghost" size="icon" onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); handleDelete(policy._id); }}><Trash2 className="w-4 h-4 text-destructive" /></Button></PermissionGate>`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyList.jsx:1050` now has a live, wired-up per-row 'Delete' `MenuItem` calling `handleDelete(record)` directly — inline single-policy delete is restored and functional (backend enforces `policy.delete` permission on the underlying `DELETE /policies/:policyId` route regardless of frontend visibility, see PM-023).

title: No cross-organization validation on `PolicyEvidence` at model level — controller checks org isolation but model allows cross-org links if controller is bypassed; pre-save hook absent
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/models/policy-evidence-link.model.js`
**Root Cause:** Controller checks org isolation but the model has no pre-save hook. Direct DB access or controller bugs could create cross-org evidence links.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add pre-save hook: `policyEvidenceLinkSchema.pre('save', async function() { const policy = await Policy.findById(this.policyId).select('organizationId'); if (!policy || String(policy.organizationId) !== String(this.organizationId)) throw new Error('Cross-organization policy evidence link rejected'); });`.
fixEvidence: Not fixed. `policy-evidence-link.model.js` (54 lines, read in full) has no `.pre('save', ...)` hook of any kind — schema, indexes, and exports only. Org-isolation still relies entirely on `policy.controller.js`'s `createEvidenceLink` controller passing `organizationId: req.orgId` correctly; there is still no model-level backstop against a cross-org link being created by a controller bug or direct DB write.

title: No cleanup job for failed S3 uploads or stuck-processing policy reader documents — failed `PolicyReaderDocument` records accumulate; processing-stuck documents persist indefinitely if Python service crashes
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy-reader.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** No scheduled job. `failed` and `processing` (stuck) `PolicyReaderDocument` records accumulate indefinitely if the Python service crashes.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Create `policy-reader-cleanup.service.js`: `await PolicyReaderDocument.deleteMany({status:'failed', createdAt:{$lt: new Date(Date.now()-7*24*60*60*1000)}});`. `await PolicyReaderDocument.updateMany({status:'processing', updatedAt:{$lt: new Date(Date.now()-30*60*1000)}}, {$set:{status:'failed', error:'Timed out — processing exceeded 30 minutes'}});`. Register as a daily BullMQ scheduled job.
fixEvidence: Partially mitigated but not fixed as described. `policy-reader.controller.js:709-770` now does REQUEST-TIME reconciliation: every `listDocuments` call detects docs stuck in `'processing'`/`'uploaded'` and triggers a background re-check of their status against the Python service (comment: 'safety net ... recover from cases where the Python callback was missed'). There is also a manual `DELETE /policy-reader/cleanup` route (line ~1050) that proxies a cleanup call to the Python side. However, neither of these is an automated, unattended scheduled job (e.g. a daily BullMQ job) — the reconciliation only fires when a user happens to open the document list, so an org that never revisits AI Reader after a crash would still accumulate stuck/failed records indefinitely, same as originally reported.

title: Error messages expose implementation details — try-catch blocks return `error.message` directly to client; may contain Mongoose internals, stack traces, or database field names
description:
**Files:** All controllers in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/`
**Root Cause:** All `catch` blocks: `res.status(500).json({error: error.message})`. Exposes Mongoose internals, validation field names, and Python error text to clients.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Create `shared/middleware/errorHandler.js`: `exports.handleError = (res, err, ctx) => { const known = err.name === 'ValidationError' ? {status:400, msg:'Validation failed'} : err.name === 'CastError' ? {status:400, msg:'Invalid ID format'} : {status:500, msg:'An unexpected error occurred'}; logger.error(ctx, err); res.status(known.status).json({error: known.msg}); };`. Replace all bare `error.message` catch responses.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The centralized handler lives at `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/errorHandler.js` (platform-wide, not policy-specific). | Policy controllers now use `asyncHandler` + `throw AppError.xxx(...)` almost exclusively (no bare `res.status(500).json({error: error.message})` pattern found anywhere in `policy.controller.js`); uncaught errors are forwarded to the global `errorHandler` middleware, which: sanitizes Mongoose `ValidationError`/`CastError`/duplicate-key (11000) errors into generic messages, and — critically — replaces ANY 500+ error's message with the generic 'Internal server error' in production (`isProduction && statusCode >= 500 ? 'Internal server error' : message`), never leaking `err.message`/stack to the client for server errors. This is the exact architecture the original fix prompt requested, implemented platform-wide rather than per-controller.

title: Draft save requires minimum 10-character content validation — same Yup constraint as publish; cannot save empty or minimal draft; defeats purpose of incremental drafting
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyCreate.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `content: Yup.string().min(10).required()` applied unconditionally regardless of `status`. Saving an empty draft is rejected with a validation error.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Change to: `content: Yup.string().when('status', { is: 'draft', then: (s) => s.optional(), otherwise: (s) => s.min(10, 'Policy content must be at least 10 characters').required('Content is required') })`. Add a distinct "Save Draft" button that sets `status = 'draft'` in Formik before submit.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: `PolicyCreate.jsx` is now a thin wrapper around `PolicyEdit.jsx`, which owns the live validation schema. | Not fixed. `PolicyEdit.jsx:344-346`: `content: Yup.string().required('Policy content is required').min(10, 'Content must be at least 10 characters')` is still applied unconditionally with no `.when('status', ...)` exemption for drafts (unlike the sibling `description` field immediately above it, which DID receive exactly this conditional treatment for PM-014). A draft still cannot be saved with empty or near-empty content.

title: Review deadline not validated for future date in backend — `submitForReview` and `requestReview` accept past deadlines; immediately-overdue reviews generate spurious escalation notifications
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/validators/policy.validation.js`
**Root Cause:** `deadline` in `reviewValidation`: `body('deadline').isISO8601()` only. No future-date check server-side. Past deadlines create immediately-overdue reviews.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add: `.custom(v => { if (v && new Date(v) <= new Date()) throw new Error('Deadline must be a future date'); return true; })` chained after `.isISO8601()` in `reviewValidation`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: There is no longer a separate `submitForReview`/`requestReview` validator — deadlines are now set via the unified `POST /policies/:policyId/transition` endpoint's `transition` validator in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy.validation.js`. | `policy.validation.js:92-114`'s `exports.transition` validator (tagged 'PM-UX-03' — same underlying fix): `body('deadline').optional().isISO8601().toDate().custom((value) => { if (value <= new Date()) { throw new Error('Review deadline must be a future date'); } return true; })` — a past deadline is now rejected server-side exactly as this defect requested, regardless of what the client sends.

title: `PolicyReaderDocument` status transitions can race on concurrent Python callbacks — no atomic precondition filter; completed status could be overwritten back to processing if callbacks arrive out of order
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy-reader.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** Status updates use plain `findByIdAndUpdate` without a precondition filter. Concurrent Python callbacks arriving out of order can overwrite a `complete` status back to `processing`.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Use precondition: `await PolicyReaderDocument.findOneAndUpdate({_id: docId, status: 'pending'}, {$set:{status:'processing'}}, {new:true})`. For completion: `await PolicyReaderDocument.findOneAndUpdate({_id: docId, status: 'processing'}, {$set:{status:'complete', results: data}}, {new:true})`. Check for `null` return to detect stale updates.
fixEvidence: Partially fixed. `policy-reader.controller.js:486-492` DOES now apply an atomic precondition filter for the initial upload→processing transition — `PolicyReaderDocument.updateOne({_id: docRecord._id, status: {$nin: ['completed','failed']}}, {$set: {jobId, status: 'processing'}})` — explicitly to avoid regressing a synchronously-completed duplicate-upload back to 'processing' (comment at line 468-472). However, the shared generic status-update helper `policy.repository.js:1176-1188`'s `updateReaderDocumentStatus()` — used by the polling-based `getStatus` flow and the background stuck-document reconciliation loop that IS the architecture today (there is no Python push-callback; status is pulled via polling, see `getStatus` at line 597) — is still a plain `findByIdAndUpdate` with no precondition filter. A completed status could still in principle be overwritten by a stale/overlapping poll response through this shared path.

title: Template engine regex fragile with escaped braces — variable/conditional/loop extraction fails for template content with literal braces (code samples, JSON); causes false variable detection
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy-template.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** `/\{\{([^}]+)\}\}/g` fails for templates containing literal braces (e.g., JSON samples, code snippets). Causes false variable detection and broken interpolation.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
`npm install handlebars`. Replace `extractVariables` with Handlebars AST walking: `const ast = Handlebars.parse(template); const vars = []; ast.body.filter(n => n.type === 'MustacheStatement').forEach(n => vars.push(n.path.original));`. Replace `interpolateTemplate` with `Handlebars.compile(template)(variables)`.
fixEvidence: Still regex-based, not a real parser. `policy-template.controller.js:15-18`'s `extractVariables` now uses `/\{\{\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\s*\}\}/g` — tightened from the original overly-permissive `[^}]+` to require a valid identifier-like key, which reduces (but does not eliminate) false positives from arbitrary double-brace occurrences in embedded code/JSON samples that happen to contain a bare identifier. No Handlebars (or other AST-based) parser was adopted. Substitution values are, however, now HTML-escaped before interpolation (`escapeHtml`, tagged PM-M06), closing off the stored-XSS angle even though the extraction fragility itself remains.

title: Reviewer existence not validated before assignment — `reviewerValidation` checks ObjectId format only, does not query DB to verify user exists and is active; non-existent reviewers silently accepted
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/validators/policy.validation.js`
**Root Cause:** `reviewerId` in `reviewValidation`: only checked for valid ObjectId format. No DB query to verify the user exists and is active. Non-existent reviewers silently accepted.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Extend `reviewerId` validator: `.custom(async v => { const u = await User.findOne({_id: v, isActive: true}).select('_id'); if (!u) throw new Error('Reviewer not found or is inactive'); return true; })`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The field is now named `assignedTo` (not `reviewerId`) and validated in the unified `exports.transition` validator in `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy.validation.js`. | Not fixed. `policy.validation.js:100-102`: `body('assignedTo').optional().isMongoId().withMessage('assignedTo must be a valid MongoDB ObjectId')` — still format-only, no `.custom()` DB lookup verifying the target user exists and is active. A malformed-but-valid-looking ObjectId for a nonexistent/deactivated user would still be accepted at the validation layer (though `assertProjectMembers`, called from `policy.controller.js`'s `transition` handler when `assignedTo` is a project-scoped assignment, does provide a partial backstop by requiring the id to be a current project member — this does not fully close the gap for org-admin-eligible reviewers who may not be project members).
